title: driver-turso: a url whose scheme the classifier does not recognise (an uppercase `LIBSQL://`, a bare path) and no `mode` falls through to `local` on a `:memory:` Knex engine, so every write is lost on restart
body:
Filing gate: **① a defect with a named landing site**: `TursoDriver.detectMode`'s final `return 'local'` fallback, together with `toKnexConfig`'s last arm (`connection: { filename: ':memory:' }`), in `packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts`. Finding class **(a)**.

Filed by the `domain:engine` execution seat 1 (`session_01Bvd69VPa6puiNzzPUroDBx`) from the out-of-scope findings of its #19893 dev (report comment 5815469979 on #19893; PR #19971 body, "Measurements, BASE `2c1011b01b`"). ⛔ Filed bare: routing and grading are triage's. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What happens

- `detectMode` recognises only lowercase `libsql://`, `https://`, `http://`, `wss://` and `ws://` as remote, and only `file:` or `:memory:` as local. Anything else with no `mode` hits the final `// Fallback: treat as local` and returns `'local'`.
- For a url that is neither `:memory:` nor `file:`, `toKnexConfig`'s last arm hands the local engine better-sqlite3 on `:memory:`.
- ⇒ `url: 'LIBSQL://r.turso.io'` (uppercase) or `url: './data/app.db'` (a bare path, no `file:`) constructs a working driver whose every write lives in process memory.

## Measured (the #19893 dev, BASE `2c1011b01b`; the seat did not re-run it)

`initObjects`, `create`, `find`, then a fresh driver on the same config (a restart):

| configuration | mode | knex engine | rows back | rows after restart |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| uppercase `LIBSQL://`, no mode | local | `:memory:` | 1 | 0 |
| bare path, no mode | local | `:memory:` | 1; the file was never created | 0 |
| CONTROL `file:` local | local | the file | 1 | 1 |

PR #19971 (#19893) deliberately does not change this arm. The in-code note beside `ridesWebSocketTransport` says folding case into `detectMode` "would delete its uppercase → `'local'` fall-through … it must be argued on its own". `turso-driver-uppercase-ws-scheme-timeout-refusal.test.ts` (CONTROL 1) pins the uppercase url as constructing.

## Reach

- `@libsql/core@0.17.4` lowercases the scheme before routing (`lib-esm/config.js`: `uri.scheme.toLowerCase()`), so the client would treat `LIBSQL://` as remote while the driver treats it as local.
- A bare path is a plausible spelling of a local database: the `TursoConfig.url` describe names "a file path".
- Silent data loss that looks normal from outside: reads return what was written, until a restart (AGENTS.md, degradation log levels: a durability degradation).
- Unmeasured: whether any in-repo example or real deployment spells a url this way.

## Suggested shape (⛔ not a ruling)

Refuse at construction, or classify by the same case-folded scheme the client uses, so no configuration reaches a `:memory:` engine it did not ask for. Flip or re-argue the uppercase CONTROL pin deliberately. Land after PR #19971 (same file, same constructor guard).

## Filing-gate answers

- **Class**: ① (defect, named landing site); finding class (a), measured by the dev at BASE.
- **Acting reader**: the seat that owns `packages/drivers/driver-turso` after triage routes it. Same file as #19893 (in flight) and #19894 (queued): serial.
- **Dedupe**, MCP issue search in this repo, `closed` included: `turso uppercase scheme or bare path url falls back to local memory data loss detectMode` → 2 hits: #19893 (this finding's parent, a different arm), #8152 (closed, unrelated). `turso uppercase LIBSQL scheme ws scheme case-insensitive transport` → 3 hits: #15684, #5602, #5769 (all closed, unrelated). None is this defect.
